verses.1:1: The pronouncement concerning Nineveh: the scroll of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
verses.1:2: The LORD is a jealous God and an avenger; the LORD is an avenger and master of fury. The LORD exacts vengeance on His foes, and He retains wrath for His enemies.
verses.1:3: The LORD is slow to anger and great in strength, yet He will surely not acquit the guilty. The LORD—His path is in whirlwind and tempest, and clouds are the dust of His feet.
verses.1:4: He rebukes the sea and dries it up, and all the rivers He parches; Bashan and Carmel languish, and the blossom of Lebanon languishes.
verses.1:5: Mountains tremble because of Him, and the hills melt away; and the earth heaves at His presence, the world and all who live in it.
verses.1:6: Before His indignation, who can stand? And who can remain standing in the burning of His anger? His fury is poured out like fire, and the rocks are shattered because of Him.
verses.1:7: Good is the LORD, a stronghold on a day of distress, and He knows those who seek refuge in Him.
verses.1:8: But with a sweeping flood He will make a full end of her place, and He will chase His enemies into darkness.
verses.1:9: What are you devising against the LORD? He Himself will make a full end; distress will not arise twice.
verses.1:10: For though entangled like thorns and drunk as from their drink, they are devoured like thoroughly dry stubble.
verses.1:11: Out of you has come forth one who devises evil against the LORD, one who counsels wickedness.
verses.1:12: This is what the LORD says: "Even if they are intact and likewise numerous, even so they will be cut down and he will pass away. And though I have afflicted you, I will not afflict you again.
verses.1:13: And now I will break his yoke bar off you, and your bonds I will tear apart."
verses.1:14: And the LORD has commanded regarding you: "No longer will anything of your name be sown; from the house of your gods I will cut off carved image and molten image. I will make your grave, because you are despicable."
verses.2:1: Look! Upon the mountains are the feet of one bringing good news, announcing peace. Observe your feasts, Judah; pay your vows, because the wicked one will not pass through you again; he is entirely cut off.
verses.2:2: A scatterer has come up against your face! Guard the rampart, watch the road, brace your loins, fortify your strength greatly.
verses.2:3: For the LORD is restoring the grandeur of Jacob, like the grandeur of Israel, because those who lay waste have laid them waste and ruined their vine branches.
verses.2:4: The shield of his warriors is dyed red; the men of valor are dressed in crimson. With fiery steel are the chariots on the day of his preparation, and the cypresses are made to quiver.
verses.2:5: In the streets the chariots rage madly; they hurtle back and forth in the broad squares. Their appearance resembles torches; like lightning bolts they dart about.
verses.2:6: He recalls his nobles; they stumble in their advance. They rush to her wall, and the protective barrier is made ready.
verses.2:7: The gates of the rivers have been opened, and the palace dissolves.
verses.2:8: And it is determined: she is laid bare, she is carried away; and her maidservants moan like the voice of doves, drumming on their breasts.
verses.2:9: And Nineveh has been like a pool of water from the days she existed, yet they are fleeing. "Stand! Stand!" Yet no one turns around.
verses.2:10: Plunder silver! Plunder gold! And there is no end to the store, riches from every treasured article.
verses.2:11: Waste, and utter waste, and devastation! Melting heart, buckling knees, and writhing anguish in all loins; and the faces of all of them gather pallor.
verses.2:12: Where is the den of lions, and the feeding ground it was for the young lions, where lion, lioness, and lion cub walked, with no one to frighten them?
verses.2:13: A lion tore enough for his cubs and strangled for his lionesses; he filled his holes with prey and his dens with torn prey.
verses.2:14: "Look, I am against you," declares the LORD of hosts, "and I will burn her chariots in smoke, and a sword will devour your young lions; I will also cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers will not be heard again."
verses.3:1: Woe to the city of bloodshed! All of her is full of deceit and plunder; prey does not depart.
verses.3:2: The sound of a whip, and the sound of a wheel's rattle, and a galloping horse, and a leaping chariot!
verses.3:3: A charging horseman, and the flash of a sword, and the gleam of a spear, and a multitude of the fallen, and a heavy mass of corpses; and there is no end to the dead bodies, and they stumble over their dead bodies—
verses.3:4: because of the abundant prostitution of a prostitute lovely in charm, mistress of sorceries, who sells nations through her prostitution and clans through her sorceries.
verses.3:5: "Look, I am against you," declares the LORD of hosts, "and I will uncover your skirts over your face, and I will show nations your nakedness and kingdoms your shame.
verses.3:6: And I will hurl filth upon you and treat you as contemptible, and I will set you like a spectacle.
verses.3:7: And it will happen that everyone who sees you will flee from you and say, 'Nineveh has been ruined! Who will mourn for her?' From where shall I seek comforters for you?"
verses.3:8: Are you any better than No-amon, who sat among the Nile canals, with waters all around her, whose rampart was the sea, and from the sea was her wall?
verses.3:9: Cush was her might, and Egypt, and there was no end; Put and the Libyans were your help.
verses.3:10: Even she went into exile, into captivity; even her young children were smashed to pieces at the head of all the streets. For her dignitaries they cast a lot, and all her great men were fastened in chains.
verses.3:11: Even you will grow drunk; you will be concealed. Even you will seek a stronghold from an enemy.
verses.3:12: All your fortresses are fig trees with early-ripe fruit; if they are shaken, they fall into the mouth of an eater.
verses.3:13: Look, your people are women in your midst! To your enemies the gates of your land have been opened wide; fire has devoured your gate bars.
verses.3:14: Draw siege water for yourself; strengthen your fortresses! Go into the mud and trample in the mortar; grasp the brick mold!
verses.3:15: There fire will devour you, a sword will cut you off; it will devour you like the young locust. Make yourself numerous like the young locust; make yourself numerous like the locust!
verses.3:16: You have multiplied your merchants beyond the stars of the sky; the young locust raids and flies away.
verses.3:17: Your crowned officials are like the locust, and your marshals are like a swarm of grasshoppers, camping in the stone walls on a day of cold. The sun shines forth, and it flees away, and its place is not known—where they are.
verses.3:18: Your shepherds slumber, king of Assyria; your nobles lie at rest. Your people are dispersed upon the mountains, and there is no one gathering them.
verses.3:19: There is no relief for your injury; grievous is your wound. All who hear the report of you clap hands over you, for upon whom has your evil not passed continually?

notes.1:3: Ketiv reads wgdwl (plene), while Qere reads ugedol-koach (defective construct form before maqqef, "great in strength"); both carry the same meaning. The Masoretic atnach divides the verse after yenaqqeh, placing the second occurrence of the divine name at the start of the second half as casus pendens ("The LORD—His path is...").
notes.1:5: The verb wattissa' ("heaves") is an unusual intransitive Qal of nasa' ("lift up, rise"), depicting the earth heaving upward before God's presence.
notes.1:8: The Masoretic text reads meqomah ("her place," referring to Nineveh). In the final clause, yeraddef-choshekh (Piel of radaph) can be read with the LORD as subject and "darkness" as adverbial goal ("He will chase His enemies into darkness") or with "darkness" as subject ("darkness will chase His enemies").
notes.1:10: The Hebrew syntax is unusually terse and elliptical, pairing 'ad-sirim sebukhim ("though entangled like thorns") with a wordplay on sava' in ukhesov'am sevu'im ("and drunk as from their drink").
notes.1:12: The Niphal perfect nagozzu (from gazaz, "shear, mow down") and the shift to third-person masculine singular we'avar ("and he will pass away," anticipating 3ms "his yoke bar" in 1:13) portray Assyria's collective might being cut down swiftly.
notes.2:1: Ketiv reads l'bwr (plene), while Qere reads la'avor-bakh (defective infinitive construct with qamets hatuf before maqqef, "to pass through you"); the meaning is unchanged.
notes.2:6: Qere reads the singular bahalikhatam ("in their advance/march"), whereas Ketiv reads the plural bhlkwtm ("in their marches/courses"). Hassokhekh (Qal active participle of sakhakh, "cover, shield") denotes a movable protective siege barrier or mantelet.
notes.2:8: A well-known crux: wehutzav is here parsed as an impersonal Hophal perfect of natzav ("and it is determined/decreed"; some take it as a proper name, Huzzab), followed by Pual gulletah ("she is laid bare," or "exiled") and Hophal ho'alatah ("she is carried away").
notes.2:9: The Masoretic phrase mime hi' (literally "from the days of she") is an elliptical temporal idiom meaning "from the days she existed" or "throughout her days."
notes.2:14: The Masoretic text abruptly shifts to a third-person feminine singular suffix in rikhvah ("her chariots") amid second-person feminine singular address, and mal'akhekheh ("your messengers") displays a unique lengthened 2fs suffix.
notes.3:3: Qere reads the weqatal wekhashelu ("and they stumble"), whereas Ketiv reads the imperfect ykshlw ("they stumble").
notes.3:8: No-amon is the Hebrew name for Egyptian Thebes (city of the god Amon). The plural ye'orim denotes the Nile and its channels, and MT miyyam ("from the sea") poetically depicts the broad river itself as the city's wall.
notes.3:9: The Masoretic text reads the second-person feminine singular be'ezratekh ("your help"), shifting into direct apostrophe to No-amon; 'otsmah lacks a mappiq in the final he, reading either as "her might" (with omitted mappiq) or as the abstract noun "might."
notes.3:16: The Qal perfect pashat ("raids") can mean either "makes a raid / spreads out to plunder" or "strips / sheds [its husk]" as the wingless young locust (yeleq) matures and flies away.
notes.3:17: Minnezarayikh ("your crowned officials") and taphserayikh ("your marshals," from Akkadian tupsharru) designate high Assyrian officials. The Masoretic text shifts from plural participle (hachonim, "camping") to collective singular (wenodad, "it flees away"; meqomo, "its place") and back to plural ('ayyam, "where they are").
